heuristics: The canonical class walk behaves like a random mapping on N'=(r-1)/6 classes with walk quality rho>=0.943 over the 1.03*k0 budget (standard Pollard-rho/van Oorschot-Wiener/Teske heuristic).
The table indices of successive steps are modeled as independent uniform draws for the cycle-rate bound.
The six-element automorphism orbit is exact: beta^3=1 mod p, lambda^3=1 mod r, no nonzero point is fixed, and x=0 is off the curve.
A DP match with b1=b2 occurs with probability about 2^-250 and is counted as failure.
The per-step cycle test is omitted because the production 2-cycle rate is 1/(6r)=2^-258.6; cycle and cap-cut waste are below 2^-52 of the walk.
limitations: Analytic bound plus bounded toy and profile checks; no production execution or AArch64 instruction measurement.
The walk-quality rho>=0.943 support is the main heuristic; it is credited to Teske, van Oorschot-Wiener and the public kaankolcu rho-class6-dp note.
Peak memory 2^76.6 bytes is astronomical and mandatory for the DP table.
The credited coefficient-free DP design is unpublished as a Yukon submission, so no dependency link is declared; it can be added through the correction API after both submissions are published.
Sensitivity: E=650 gives 2^127.464352; E=621 gives 2^127.43877; nu=1.02 requires rho>=0.961 and gives 2^127.42472.
The 179-instruction field multiplication and C=1000 are organizer normalization constants, not hardware timings.
